common_name: Seminole Wind Daylily (Parent of Belle Cook)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Seminole Wind is a Hemerocallis cultivar documented chiefly as one of the two parents, crossed with Ed Brown, behind Malcolm Brooker's 2001 introduction Belle Cook. No detailed description of Seminole Wind's own flower color or form survives in the sources consulted, a common gap for breeding-line parent cultivars overshadowed by their offspring. Grow it, as with other tetraploid daylily lines, in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to sustain vigorous flowering.

directions: Baby Darling is a Hemerocallis cultivar documented as one of the grandparents behind Darrel A.
